records.title: 2026 National Defense Strategy
records.direction: Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.
records.change_summary: Homeland defence moves to the first priority; industrial base becomes a line of effort in its own right.
records.check: PDF не прочитан (403 для автоматического чтения, текст PDF в браузере недоступен без скачивания). Четыре линии — по вторичным сводкам и war.gov (история 12.05.2026 говорит о supercharging industrial capacity). Дату и формулировки сверить по тексту PDF.

records.title: PAC-3 MSE framework agreement under the Acquisition Transformation Strategy
records.direction: Seven-year framework agreements for proven munitions, giving industry long-term demand so it invests in capacity; PAC-3 MSE output to rise from about 600 to about 2,000 a year, subject to Congress.
records.change_summary: Shift from year-to-year buys to seven-year demand signals; the same model to be applied to multiple munitions contracts over the next year, with seven-year subcontracts for key suppliers.
records.anchor_quote: This facilitization strategy will be applied to multiple munitions procurement contracts over the next year, pending Congressional appropriations, to replenish our stockpiles

records.title: President's Fiscal Year 2027 Defense Budget request
records.direction: Record $1.5 trillion request (+42%) with funding to expand production and stockpiles of Patriot, THAAD, precision strike missiles and midrange weapons; multiyear contracts of up to seven years for critical munitions.
records.change_summary: Multiyear authority extended to up to seven years; the department says it will request multiyear authority wherever it expects to keep buying a system.
records.anchor_quote: the department also looks to expand multiyear contracts up to seven years for critical munitions
records.check: Сумма на 12/14 приоритетных боеприпасов Munitions Acceleration Council (~$52,9 млрд) — только в PDF Comptroller (не прочитан); в синтез не брать без чтения.

records.title: SM-6 multiyear procurement award (Department of the Navy)
records.direction: Navy commits to a multiyear SM-6 buy (five years plus two options, up to $24.4 billion) to give industry a stable demand signal, expand production and build magazine depth.
records.change_summary: Follows the Tomahawk award; part of the PAE Munitions effort to accelerate production of critical weapons.
records.anchor_quote: The SM-6 contract establishes a multi-year procurement commitment
records.check: Официальный релиз ВМС НЕ называет пополнение запасов после Ближнего Востока — это формулировка Defense News. В EXAMPLE_01 §10 это указано как «официальное обоснование» — исправить при использовании.

records.title: Our North, Strong and Free: A Renewed Vision for Canada's Defence
records.direction: Asserting sovereignty in the Arctic and northern regions is named the most urgent defence task: northern operational support hubs, coastal and underwater sensors, a High Arctic satellite ground station and improved satellite capabilities.
records.change_summary: Arctic moves to the top of Canada's defence priorities, backed by C$8.1 billion over five years and C$73 billion over 20 years.
records.anchor_quote: The most urgent and important task we face is asserting Canada's sovereignty in the Arctic and northern regions
records.check: Дата 08.04.2024 — по релизу Премьер-министра (pm.gc.ca, 2024/04/08); страница резюме датирована 17.04.2024.

records.title: Canada's Arctic Foreign Policy
records.direction: Canada will continue to assert its sovereignty and take a comprehensive approach to Arctic security, with foreign and defence policy working together.
records.change_summary: Diplomatic counterpart to Our North, Strong and Free.
records.anchor_quote: To achieve its objective of a stable, prosperous and secure Arctic, Canada will continue to assert its sovereignty.
records.check: Точная дата публикации на странице не указана (только 2024); 06.12.2024 — по памяти, сверить.

records.title: Security, Sovereignty and Prosperity: Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy
records.direction: Build, partner, buy: build at home in areas of sovereign capability, partner with allies, buy abroad only when neither is feasible; raise the share of defence acquisitions awarded to Canadian firms to 70%, with the Defence Investment Agency at the centre.
records.change_summary: Canada's first defence industrial strategy; 'Buy Canadian' becomes the guiding rule for defence acquisitions.
records.anchor_quote: raise the share of defence acquisitions awarded to Canadian firms to 70%
records.check: Полный текст стратегии: canada.ca .../industrial-strategy/security-sovereignty-prosperity.html (не читался целиком).

records.title: Enhanced Satellite Communications Project – Polar (ESCP-P): Mil-Ka contract to Telesat
records.direction: Defence Investment Agency awards Telesat about C$2.3 billion (plus options of about C$214 million and C$218 million) for sovereign Arctic military satellite communications, as the BUILD component of the Defence Industrial Strategy.
records.change_summary: Puts the strategy's BUILD component into a contract; the government says secure Arctic connectivity arrives years earlier than originally planned.
records.anchor_quote: The contract will defend Canadian sovereignty in the Arctic
records.check: «15 лет» и начало сервиса в 2028 — только у Telesat, не в релизе правительства. Это событие-контракт, а не доктрина: в справочнике как реализация CA-01/CA-03.

records.title: White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan
records.direction: Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.
records.change_summary: National escape clause of the Stability and Growth Pact for defence (up to 1.5% of GDP a year for four years) and a new EU loan instrument, SAFE, of up to €150 billion.
records.anchor_quote: the Commission will raise up to €150 billion on the capital markets
records.check: Дата 19.03.2025 — по заголовку/поиску, на странице пресс-релиза дата текстом не извлечена; перечень семи областей — по поисковой сводке, фраза со страницы не извлечена.

records.title: Council Regulation establishing the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument
records.direction: Up to €150 billion in EU loans for member states investing in defence industrial production through common procurement of priority capabilities.
records.change_summary: First large-scale EU-level defence investment programme; loans in principle require common procurement by at least two countries; Ukraine and EEA-EFTA industries can take part.
records.anchor_quote: support those member states that wish to invest in defence industrial production through common procurement, focusing on priority capabilities

records.title: Preserving Peace – Defence Readiness Roadmap 2030
records.direction: Milestones towards full EU defence readiness by 2030, with four flagships: European Drone Defence Initiative, Eastern Flank Watch, European Air Shield and European Space Shield.
records.change_summary: Moves from financing (ReArm Europe) to concrete joint projects; an EU-wide military mobility area by 2027 and a single defence market with harmonised rules by 2030.
records.anchor_quote: the Roadmap proposes four European Flagships: the European Drone Defence Initiative, the Eastern Flank Watch, the European Air Shield, and the European Space Shield

records.title: The Hague Summit Declaration
records.direction: Allies commit to 5% of GDP a year by 2035: at least 3.5% on core defence requirements and up to 1.5% on broader security spending, including the defence industrial base.
records.change_summary: Replaces the 2% guideline; commitment to rapidly expand transatlantic defence industrial cooperation; trajectory reviewed in 2029.
records.anchor_quote: Allies commit to invest 5% of GDP annually on core defence requirements
records.check: Цитата получена через автоматическое чтение (WebFetch), не через браузер; при загрузке сверить формулировку.

records.title: Strategic Defence Review 2025 – Making Britain Safer: secure at home, strong abroad
records.direction: Move to warfighting readiness: £6bn on munitions this Parliament with an 'always on' pipeline and at least six new energetics and munitions factories; up to £1bn for homeland air and missile defence; a Digital Targeting Web by 2027; more autonomy and uncrewed systems; up to 12 SSN-AUKUS submarines; a new CyberEM Command.
records.change_summary: Shift towards networks of crewed, uncrewed and autonomous assets and an always-on munitions industrial base.
records.anchor_quote: building at least six new energetics and munitions factories in the UK
records.check: Дата 02.06.2025 — по поиску; HTML-страница показывает только «Updated 8 July 2025».

records.title: Defence Industrial Strategy 2025: Making Defence an Engine for Growth
records.direction: Reform procurement, innovate at wartime pace and grow the UK industrial base so industry can deliver the Strategic Defence Review.
records.change_summary: Defence becomes the sector plan of the UK Modern Industrial Strategy, with priority outcomes on UK-based businesses, resilience and procurement reform.
records.anchor_quote: we will reform procurement, innovate at wartime pace, and grow our industrial base

records.title: Bundeswehr Planning and Procurement Acceleration Act (BwPBBG)
records.direction: Faster planning and procurement so that equipment and materiel reach the troops sooner, as the Bundeswehr refocuses on national and alliance defence and grows.
records.change_summary: Joint bill of the economy and defence ministries (cabinet 23.07.2025) passed by the Bundestag on 15.01.2026.
records.anchor_quote: Es soll dazu beitragen, dass Gerät, Ausrüstung und Material in Zukunft schneller bei der Truppe ankommen.
records.check: Срок до 2035, отмена деления на лоты, прямые закупки и авансы — только по поисковой сводке; на странице BMVg нет. В синтез не брать без чтения текста закона.

records.title: Actualisation de la loi de programmation militaire 2024-2030
records.direction: €36 billion extra for the armed forces in 2026–2030 on top of the €413 billion LPM: nuclear deterrence, air defence, counter-drone, deep strike, munitions, drones, space and electromagnetic warfare.
records.change_summary: Munitions +€8.5 billion (+53%) to raise stocks and industrial production capacity; space +€3.9 billion; counter-drone systems for every unit in the short term.
records.anchor_quote: L’effort sur les munitions est majeur, avec 8,5 milliards d’euros supplémentaires
records.check: Год промульгации (16 августа) на странице не указан, дата страницы — 27.11.2025, что противоречит; по поиску проект представлен 08.04.2026 → вероятно 16.08.2026. Сверить по Légifrance.

records.change_summary: Netherlands moves to structural compliance with the 2% norm and heavier land capabilities at NATO's request.

records.title: NSPM: Rebuilding the United States Navy and America's Shipbuilding Industrial Base
records.direction: Fix long-term problems in Navy shipbuilding and repair: a fifth Naval shipyard, a submarine Component Repair Center, reorganisation of NAVSEA and direct investment in shipyards on the 'Finland model'.
records.change_summary: Foreign shipbuilders investing in US yards may temporarily build up to two ships abroad; CVN-81 returns to steam catapults and hydraulic elevators.
records.anchor_quote: The Memorandum directs the Secretary of War to establish a fifth Naval shipyard, the first in over 80 years
records.check: Источник — fact sheet Белого дома, текст меморандума не читался.

records.title: Executive Order on securing defense supply chains and domestic acquisition of critical materials
records.direction: Fewer waivers for critical materials from covered nations, mandatory supply-chain mapping for critical defence supply chains, and qualification of new domestic and partner-nation sources.
records.change_summary: Builds on the March 2025 mineral-production order; puts the burden on defence contractors to requalify suppliers away from adversary sources.
records.anchor_quote: The Order limits circumstances in which the Secretary of Defense should issue waivers for critical materials from covered nations
